editorial:
Imagine getting a job where you just count people in small towns, but then you find a place that makes zero sense. You follow a census-taker who visits a tiny village that has had exactly 436 people for a whole century. No one is born, no one dies, and no one leaves. The vibe is super creepy from the start because the locals are way too friendly, and everything feels like a trap. You will feel the tension build as you realize that the town isn't just weird, it is actually dangerous for any outsider who wanders in.

The acting is solid and the slow build-up of the mystery keeps you guessing until the end. While some parts might feel a bit slow, the big reveal makes the wait worth it. If you love stories about strange cults and secret rules, you should definitely check this one out. Since it is an older movie, it looks best if you can find a high-quality version. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend night.
endingExplained: You find out the town is actually a purgatory for people who committed terrible crimes. They are forced to live there as a punishment. The twist is that the population must stay at 436, so when a new person arrives, an old resident gets to leave the town and go back to the real world. The main character discovers the horror of this cycle and has to fight to escape before he becomes a permanent part of the count.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves mysteries about strange towns and secret societies.
